summary: Akshay Ramanlal Desai worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Mumbai from circa 1936 to 1946, working under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye between circa 1941 and 1946.

Alain Daniélou was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at St. John's College and Banaras Hindu University. He held directorships at the French Institute of Pondicherry, Adyar Library, and comparative music institutes in Berlin and Venice.

Alaka Chudal is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She was a lecturer at Nepal Sanskrit University (1995–2007), completed her PhD at the University of Vienna (2009–2014), and held a post at the University of Vienna in 2007.

Alan Avdagić is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Jena and the University of Würzburg, held a post at Würzburg, and was attested at the Free University of Berlin in 2026.
Alan Butterworth was active in Indology and history/archaeology. He was educated at Elizabeth College from circa 1878 to 1883 and studied at Balliol College, Oxford, in 1883.

Alan Coates Bouquet was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at University College London, Trinity College, Cambridge, and Jesus College, Cambridge. He served as Lecturer in History and Comparative Study of Religion at Cambridge from 1924 to 1955.

Alan Entwistle worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Southampton, SOAS University of London (under J. C. Wright), and under Jacob Ensink. He held posts at the University of Groningen and the University of Washington.

Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Johns Hopkins University and Temple University, and has held professorships in philosophy at the University of Delaware between 1990 and 2014.

Alan Gerard Wagner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Parimal G. Patil (attested 2008) and also studied under Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.
Alan Gowans was a scholar of history and archaeology. He completed his studies at the University of Toronto in 1946 and at Princeton University in 1948 and 1950.

Alan John Bayard Wace was an archaeologist and historian. Educated at Pembroke College under Robert Alexander Neil, he held posts at the British School at Athens (1914–1923), Victoria and Albert Museum (1924–1934), Cambridge (1934–1944), and Alexandria University (circa 1943–1952).
Alan Lomax pursued education at Choate Rosemary Hall, St. Mark's School of Texas, Harvard University (circa 1932–1933), the University of Texas at Austin (circa 1933–1936), and Columbia University.
Alan Nussbaum is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Harvard University from circa 1970 to 1976 and became a professor at Cornell University in 1985.

Alan Sponberg was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from the University of British Columbia. He held academic posts at Princeton University, Stanford University, the Library of Congress, and the University of Montana.

Alan Watts worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Bexley Seabury Seminary and under various teachers, he held posts at Northwestern University, the American Academy of Asian Studies, Harvard, San Jose State, and the Esalen Institute.

Alasdair MacIntyre is a philosopher who studied at Queen Mary University of London and the University of Manchester. He held academic appointments at the University of Essex, Brandeis University, the University of Notre Dame, Duke University, and London Metropolitan University.

Alasdair Urquhart is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh and the University of Pittsburgh. He held posts at the University of Toronto Mississauga (1973–1975) and served as Emeritus Professor at the University of Toronto (1986).

Alastair Gornall is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge (2009–2013). He held posts at SUTD, SOAS University of London, and the Pali Text Society.

Albert Benjamin Norton worked in linguistics and Indology. He completed his studies at Northwestern University from circa 1867 to 1871 and at Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary from circa 1871 to 1872.

Albert Cuny was a linguist who earned his PhD at the Sorbonne, studying under Antoine Meillet, Victor Henry, and Sylvain Lévi. He taught at Lycée Edmond Perrier and the University of Paris before serving as a professor at the University of Bordeaux.
